entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Munju was the 22nd king of Baekje, one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, reigning from 475 to 477 CE. His brief but tumultuous tenure marked a critical turning point in Baekje history, characterized by profound internal disunity and the devastating loss of the Hanseong (present-day Seoul) capital to the rival Goguryeo kingdom. This catastrophic defeat, which occurred just prior to his ascension, forced Baekje to relocate its capital southward, initiating a period of strategic vulnerability and political fragmentation that fundamentally reshaped the geopolitical landscape of the Korean Peninsula.

Ascending to the throne amidst the ruins of Baekje's northern territories, Munju inherited a kingdom in crisis. The 475 CE assault by Goguryeo's King Jangsu had not only seized Hanseong but also resulted in the death of Munju's father, King Gaero. Munju's initial actions included moving the capital to Ungjin (modern-day Gongju), a more defensible mountainous region, signaling a shift from Baekje's traditional power base in the Han River basin. Despite this strategic retreat, his reign was plagued by the persistent influence of powerful aristocrats, particularly the Hae and Jin clans, whose internecine struggles and challenges to royal authority severely hampered any efforts at national reconstruction or military resurgence against Goguryeo's continued southward expansion. His attempts to consolidate power and stabilize the kingdom were largely thwarted by the entrenched factionalism within the Baekje court.
